content:
It feels like the carbon fiber is acting like graphite in this part and lubricating the screw as it goes in. It’s easy to over tighten as a result. I had to look at the screw as I tightened it and make sure it was completely flush with the metal face.

Definitely do not use an electric screwdriver on this part!
The mounting holes in my vent-lever holder were a tad too large, and the screws do not snug all the way up.  Will probably need to reprint this part after the whole thing is running.

My Vent-lever-holder split along the layer lines adjacent to the screw hole almost immediately when installing the screw. It would probably be a good idea to run an M3 tap into this hole beforehand, if you have one.

I was still able to get the screw snug, so re-printing this part will be relegated to the list of things to print when I’m absolutely bored out of my mind and have nothing better to do; it will suffice for now.
mind the metal feathers when screwing in the two svrews. dont place the part on them.

Same issues as others I think the part tolerance is a bit too big on these holes as I did not get great positive "tight" when I got to the end like on every other part so far. Watch out to go until the part doesn't move and don't keep tightening!

I was unable to tighten any of three the screws into the vent-lever holder part (i.e., the screws  kept spinning, no purchase at the end). Not sure if the screw hole tolerances on this part are off, but that was my experience.

replies.content: same. They never got tight. Immedately spun through..
It worked for me. Probably a bad batch.
